Hi, again i am new to the copy number estimation from snp data, so i
am sorry if my questiones are really naive:

for my 7 sample of affy snp 6.0 data. But instead of going through the
segmentation step, I want to generate a report of these raw copy
number in the format of snp_id, log(CN)

So here are my questions:
1-- I think the raw copy number is alreay in log scale, right?
2-- what would I need to do to map x to the snp_id? -- as i remember
there was some utility method from bioconductor that do similar
mapping for affymetrix's expression data set. Do we have these for the
snp data?
3-- These are the CN for each probe, not the probe set, right?

messages.author: 9dda904b2c7a149c
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] raw copy number report
parts:
On Sat, Jul 26, 2008 at 3:06 AM, yupu <yupu...@gmail.com> wrote:

[snip]

> So here are my questions:
> 1-- I think the raw copy number is alreay in log scale, right?
> 2-- what would I need to do to map x to the snp_id? -- as i remember
> there was some utility method from bioconductor that do similar
> mapping for affymetrix's expression data set. Do we have these for the
> snp data?
> 3-- These are the CN for each probe, not the probe set, right?

1. Yes.
2. You will have to go back to the annotation files provided by
Affymetrix. There is a CSV file available from the netaffx website
for each SNP chip and this contains information such as SNP IDs.
There was a discussion on this issue a few days ago (try searching the
group archive).
3. No, they are for the probe set (unit). See the discussion on
"Extract raw copy number using Aroma" from last week.

Cheers,

Ken
